answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, giving voting weight only to paths reached from trusted seeds. A sybil cluster can be internally dense, but few external attestations form a sparse cut with low conductance; under normalized walk weighting, limited probability flow across that boundary caps its aggregate influence instead of letting fabricated identities multiply votes. An ember of genuine trust cannot turn a relic of isolated accounts into an unlimited voyage of authority.
